title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government outlines its response to the 2020 Committee report on AI and public standards, emphasizing the need for clear, evidence‑based guidelines that promote safe, transparent, and accountable AI use. It announces a framework to develop and enforce these standards, including measures to protect privacy, ensure fairness, and encourage innovation while safeguarding the public interest.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual outlines its strategy for overseeing AI use in qualifications, aiming to maintain fairness, integrity, and transparency in exams and assessments. The document was issued in response to requests from the education, science and business ministries to address the impact of AI on the qualifications sector.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyright laws affect the use of copyrighted materials in training AI systems. It assesses the legal and practical implications for creators, developers, and users, offering guidance on compliance and fair use.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s AI report, “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency.” It outlines plans to strengthen policy, regulation, and investment to address the report’s concerns and promote safe, responsible AI use.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the purpose, scope, and responsibilities for a committee tasked with examining how artificial intelligence should be governed in the public sector. It also includes FAQs to clarify common questions about the review process.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on the governance of artificial intelligence, outlining its perspective on AI regulation and oversight. The submission addresses key issues such as accountability, transparency, and ethical standards in AI development.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy explains how AI technologies will change the rules for medical products, emphasizing safety, effectiveness, and transparency. It adopts the AI White Paper principles to guide regulators, industry, and stakeholders in setting standards for AI‑powered diagnostics, therapeutics, and medical devices, ensuring accountability and public trust.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy outlines how the organisation plans to become the leading AI‑powered defence entity worldwide, prioritising effectiveness, efficiency, trust, and influence. It sets a vision of being the most capable, reliable and influential defence organisation for its size, guiding development and deployment of AI across defence operations.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport AI Action Plan explains how the UK Department for Transport (DfT) will partner with the transport industry to harness the benefits of artificial intelligence, such as improved safety and efficiency. It also outlines strategies for mitigating risks, including data privacy concerns and system reliability.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report tracks how copyright-protected materials are being used to train and develop AI systems under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It provides an update on compliance, challenges, and progress made in balancing intellectual‑property rights with AI innovation.
